transcript:
Meeting header:
- Date/Time: 2027-09-14 09:00 PDT
- Duration: ~52 minutes
- Attendees: Jared Lin (Redwood AE), Maya Singh (Redwood SE), Olivia Grant (Penumbra Head of AI), Marco Ruiz (Penumbra Lead Eng), Sofia Park (Penumbra Head of Security)

Summary:
Quick discovery: Penumbra Retail is evaluating hosted vs Dedicated vs Private for an LLM feature that summarizes long multi-page receipts and calls point-of-sale tools. They want open model comparisons, 32k+ context support for batching many receipts together, multilingual (EN/ES/FR/JA), and secure handling of PCI and PII with KMS and SSO.

Topics:
- Model candidates (Llama family, Mistral variants, Llama-3-70B qlora, local fine-tunes)
- Context length needs (8k vs 32k vs 100k for receipts + transaction history)
- Tool-calling: inventory lookup, refund actions, POS tool integration (webhooks/ops)
- Deployment: hosted for quick test, Dedicated for predictable throughput, Private/VPC for PCI-scope
- Security: SOC 2, KMS, SSO/SAML, audit logs

Action items (captured in notes): send pricing, security pack, benchmark plan

Transcript body:
[00:00] Jared (Redwood AE): hey everyone, thanks for joining. quick intros — i'm jared, i run solutions/partnerships for redwood inference. maya's our se, she'll dive into infra details.
[00:15] Olivia (Penumbra): hi all, i'm olivia, head of ai at penumbra. we've been prototyping on prem and cloud, want to see what redwood offers.
[00:28] Marco (Penumbra): marco here, i'll be doing the engineering work if we move forward.
[00:34] Maya (Redwood SE): hi, thanks. can you give a quick sense of the primary user flow?
[00:40] Olivia: sure — customers upload receipts (photos or pdfs), we normalize, extract line items, totals, taxes, then create a summarized view + recommended actions (refund, loyalty points). we also need cross-receipt context: the last 12 transactions per customer. so sometimes a single request is actually 6-8 receipts concatenated.
[01:05] Marco: and we have multi-language receipts, spanish and french are common, some japanese for tourist purchases.
[01:13] Sofia (Penumbra): security question up front — a lot of the dataset is PCI-related, card last4, some tokenized data. we need key management and auditability.
[01:23] Jared: understood. typical things we see — teams start with hosted to iterate then go to dedicated or private when latency/cost/scope matter. what are your primary success criteria?
[01:36] Olivia: accuracy on line-item extraction > 95% and latency under 800ms p95 for single receipt; for batched multi-receipts p95 under 1.5s ideally. cost target is, uh, under $0.01 per receipt if possible, but we know cost varies with model and tokens.
[01:58] Maya: cool. are you leaning toward closed models (OpenAI) or open models?
[02:04] Olivia: prefer open models so we can fine-tune occasionally and avoid vendor lock. also cost control.
[02:11] Jared: makes sense. quick list of candidates we typically evaluate: Llama-3 variants (35B/70B), Mistral-Instruct-like models, and quantized qlora tuned versions. there was a mention of local mistral — that sometimes surfaces.
[02:28] Marco: yep, we've tested Mistral locally, but performance on 70B is... heavy, and our infra team is wary.
[02:36] Maya: a couple of technical notes that affect your choice: tokenizer overhead for receipts is high because of numeric sequences and tables, kv cache sizes blow up with long contexts if you use naive concatenation, and batching strategies matter for cost.
[02:53] Jared: also, redwood's runtime supports automatic prefix caching for repeated front-matter like store metadata, and continuous batching to hit latency SLOs while saving tokens.
[03:06] Olivia: can you explain prefix caching again? sometimes the docs are dense.
[03:10] Maya: sure — if you have a repeated header or template across receipts, we cache the encoded keys so you don't re-encode every token for each request. on long contexts this cuts CPU/GPU time. it's not magic but it's helpful.
[03:24] Marco: that sounds useful. question — we want 32k context to append receipts plus 2 years of transaction history per customer. do you support 100k contexts anywhere?
[03:35] Maya: natively we support a few context windows depending on model variants; for 100k you usually stitch results or use retrieval/embedding to fetch relevant history instead of sending everything. we can run experiments with extended context models — there are tradeoffs in latency and memory.
[03:49] Olivia: hmm, so for very long chains you suggest retrieval-augmented approach?
[03:53] Maya: yes, we'd recommend chunking and embeddings for long histories. for the in-shot multi-receipt summarization (6-8 receipts) 32k is sufficient for most cases.
[04:03] Jared: i want to raise deployment options — hosted is fastest to start and gives you model catalog access. Dedicated gives predictable GPU and can reduce cost at scale; Private/VPC is what customers pick when they need full network isolation and to bring their own KMS. Sofia, does that align with your security needs?
[04:20] Sofia: possibly — PCI scope is our main driver. We need audit logs, customer-managed KMS/HSM, and SSO with SAML for ops. Do you have SOC 2?
[04:32] Jared: yes, we have SOC 2 Type II, and detailed KMS integration docs — we'll share. we also have per-token audit logs and route-level tracing.
[04:42] Marco: for a pilot we'd probably start hosted, but lock to Dedicated if latency or data policies require. what's the difference in latency between hosted shared pool and dedicated 4xA100?
[04:53] Maya: shared pools have variability, but at p95 for typical 35B models you might see ~400–700ms; Dedicated with reserved capacity generally halves tail latency and gives throughput guarantees. exact numbers depend on sequence length and batch.
[05:09] Olivia: pricing question — can you give a ballpark for token cost on a 70B qlora hosted vs dedicated?
[05:17] Jared: ballparks: hosted qlora variants could be ~ $0.0008–0.002 per 1k tokens (varies by model). Dedicated amortizes GPU cost so effective per-token is lower at steady high throughput — we'll send a comparative sheet with our 4-GPU and 8-GPU profiles.
[05:34] Marco: do you support tool-calling? we plan to have a read/write tool to our inventory and refunds microservice.
[05:41] Maya: yes. we support function-style tool calls and structured outputs. you can configure safe-mode for actions (dry-run) and allow redwood's runtime to call webhooks into your services. we also have a retry/fallback policy if the tool times out.
[05:55] Olivia: and how are tool calls authenticated? we can't expose production creds.
[06:00] Maya: we usually recommend a short-lived credential proxy or signed webhooks, plus RBAC on the plane. in Dedicated/Private you can put the runtime in your VPC and use internal IAM.
[06:12] Sofia: for PCI we need to ensure those calls don't leak card data in logs. are logs redacted?
[06:18] Jared: yes, we have token-level redaction options and configurable retention. plus in Private you can keep logs within your network.
[06:26] Marco: curious about fine-tuning — we may want to do periodic qlora style fine-tunes for our receipt templates. does Redwood host finetuning or do we manage?
[06:37] Maya: we can host fine-tune flows for you on Dedicated or Private; for strict compliance customers often run fine-tunes in their environment and then we import the model artifact. both are supported.
[06:48] Olivia: one more on multilingual — do you recommend one model for all languages or language-specific models?
[06:55] Maya: depends. Many 70B instruction-tuned models handle multilingual okay, but you might get better accuracy with region-specific fine-tune data. we usually recommend starting with a single multilingual base and add language-specific fine-tunes if you see regressions.
[07:09] Marco: do you have any runbooks or reference benchmarks we can look at?
[07:13] Jared: yes, we have a benchmarking repo and an ops runbook. i'll share links after.
[07:18] Olivia: for the pilot we want to evaluate on three tasks: extraction accuracy, summarization quality, and tool-calling reliability. sample size 10k receipts/day for 7 days.
[07:29] Maya: noted — for throughput we'll recommend a Dedicated 4-GPU pool for that scale as a starting point; cost estimates will follow.
[07:36] Marco: ok, small nit — we've seen tokenization mismatch between tokenizer forks (eg: llama vs open-sourced tokenizers) which causes token count variance. do you lock tokenizers per model?
[07:47] Maya: we lock a tokenizer per model in our catalog; if you bring a custom model we validate and freeze the tokenizer to avoid drift.
[07:54] Olivia: what about routing policies? we sometimes want to route low-latency simple requests to smaller models and heavy batch jobs to bigger models.
[08:02] Jared: our smart routing supports policy-based routing by cost/latency/regional endpoints — you can set a funnel: small model for quick lookups, high-capacity reserved model for heavy batches, with automatic fallback.
[08:17] Marco: any limitations on concurrent tool-calls per request? like calling inventory plus refunds in one interaction?
[08:23] Maya: you can do multiple calls; we serialize or parallelize based on your workflow. the runtime gives a per-request trace so you can debug.
[08:33] Olivia: great. security again — SSO integration timeline and support for SCIM?
[08:39] Jared: we support SAML 2.0 SSO and SCIM for provisioning in Dedicated and Private, hosted has SSO via SAML as well. we'll include a setup guide.
[08:50] Sofia: who would we talk to on the infra side for networking and VPC peering if we go private?
[08:55] Maya: our private deployment team coordinates VPC peering and on-prem packages; i can loop in the private infra PM in the follow-up.
[09:05] Olivia: can you walk through an example of latency and token cost for a 6-receipt batch using a 70B qlora?
[09:11] Maya: rough example — 6 receipts ~ average 2k tokens after OCR + normalization. so input 12k tokens and output 300 tokens. with a qlora 70B on Dedicated you might see end-to-end 900–1200ms p95; token cost depends on quantization but it's in the higher band. we'll produce a concrete spreadsheet.
[09:34] Marco: for evaluation metrics we want confusion matrix for item classification and false positives on refunds. can you capture structured eval outputs?
[09:41] Maya: yes, Redwood Optimize supports attaching evals to rollouts and setting regression alerts.
[09:48] Olivia: what's the expected timeline from pilot to prod for you customers?
[09:52] Jared: typically 4–8 weeks: 1 week pilot, 2–3 weeks iterate models and prompts, then Dedicated provisioning + load testing. Private adds provisioning time (networking, security sign-off).
[10:04] Marco: ok. small thing — how do we handle customer PII deletion requests in logs?
[10:09] Sofia: (overlap) it's a compliance requirement.
[10:11] Jared: we have API-level deletion and retention windows; we can support e-discovery and export of logs for audits.
[10:18] Olivia: good. Anything else for the pilot?
[10:21] Maya: we'll need a sample dataset (masked where needed) and a short doc of your success criteria. i'll draft a benchmark plan.
[10:28] Jared: and i'll send pricing and SOC2/KMS/SSO docs.
[10:32] Olivia: perfect. thanks both.
[10:35] Sofia: thanks.
[10:37] Marco: thanks.

(End of main discussion)

Quick recap (verbatim):
- Pilot: 7 days, 10k receipts/day, evaluate extraction/summarization/tool-calling.
- Suggested infra: start hosted for iteration then Dedicated 4-GPU for pilot throughput.
- Security: share SOC2, KMS options, scoping for PCI.

Notes on transcription quality: occasional mislabels and minor word swaps (e.g., 'qlora' sometimes transcribed as 'cola' in auto captions).
